name: AL-01
label: Safe R

key_factors: Strong Republican district (R+17 partisan lean) after redistricting
Jerry Carl's large fundraising edge ($1.16M vs $86K) plus outside support
Prediction markets price Democratic chances at about 3%
model.rationale: The district's deep Republican lean and Carl's overwhelming financial advantage leave Clyde Jones with no evident path; markets and fundamentals align on a comfortable Republican win.
model.watch: Any late polling showing the race unexpectedly competitive would be the main signal to revisit.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; fundamentals point clearly one way (post-redistricting), so it is treated as safe for that party.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Alabama's 1st District is an open seat after redistricting, and its partisan lean of roughly seventeen points Republican makes it difficult terrain for a Democrat. Jerry Carl, the Republican, has raised over $1.1 million and holds a large cash advantage, with more than half a million dollars in outside spending on his behalf. Clyde Jones has raised under $90,000 with no reported outside support.

No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, so the outlook rests on fundamentals and money, both of which point the same way. Prediction markets give the Democrat only a small chance. The race is rated Safe Republican.
